title: Consent for stroke thrombolysis
stem: Resus 4. Mrs Au, 65, developed left arm and leg weakness and slurred speech while having breakfast, 80 minutes ago. BP 196/112, glucose 7.0. NIHSS 9. Non-contrast CT brain shows no bleed. She is alert. Discuss thrombolysis with her and check for contraindications.
notes:
Checked against the European Stroke Organisation guidelines (ESO 2021 on IV thrombolysis; ESO 2023 expedited recommendation on tenecteplase), AHA/ASA 2019 acute ischaemic stroke guideline (with 2026 update where relevant), NICE NG128 (updated 2022/2023), and Hong Kong Hospital Authority stroke thrombolysis practice.

IV thrombolysis for disabling ischaemic stroke within 4.5 hours of onset (or last known well): alteplase 0.9 mg/kg (max 90 mg, 10% bolus, rest over 1 hour) or tenecteplase 0.25 mg/kg single bolus (max 25 mg), now an equal or preferred option in ESO and NICE. Beyond 4.5 hours or wake-up stroke: selected patients with imaging mismatch. Large vessel occlusion (CT angiogram): mechanical thrombectomy up to 6 hours, and up to 24 hours with imaging selection. BP must be under 185/110 before and 180/105 for 24 hours after.

Benefit: about 10 more patients per 100 treated within 3 hours have little or no disability, fewer at 3–4.5 hours; symptomatic ICH about 6% versus 1% (NINDS-era figures; lower in modern registries).

Your notes use a 3-hour window and the NINDS numbers; the window is now 4.5 hours, tenecteplase is an accepted alternative, and CT angiography for thrombectomy should be part of the plan. Your contraindication lists (older ECASS-III warnings after 3 hours: age over 80, diabetes with prior stroke, NIHSS over 25) are no longer absolute in AHA 2019.

steps.label: Check eligibility
steps.hint: Exact onset, anticoagulants, bleeding, surgery, previous stroke or bleed, pregnancy.

Onset.t: When exactly did this start? When were you last normal?
Onset.r: At 07:40, at breakfast. I was fine a second before.

Bleeding risk.r: No. Just blood pressure tablets — I sometimes forget them.

Bleeding risk.t: Any recent bleeding, surgery, head injury or stroke?
Bleeding risk.mark: Asks about recent bleeding, surgery, trauma and stroke

Bleeding risk.t: Ever had a brain bleed, aneurysm or brain tumour?
Bleeding risk.mark: Asks about previous ICH or intracranial lesion

Other.r: No allergies. Fully independent, still working.

steps.label: Talk to the nurse
steps.hint: Lower BP below 185/110 before thrombolysis; CT angiogram; weight.

opts.t: Labetalol 10 mg IV now to get the BP below 185/110
CT angiogram now for a large vessel occlusion; call the stroke team
opts.mark: CT angiography for thrombectomy and stroke team activation

opts.r: No antiplatelets for 24 hours after thrombolysis.

steps.label: Discuss with Mrs Au
steps.hint: Diagnosis, the drug, benefit, risk, time-critical, questions.

opts.t: You've had a stroke — a clot blocking blood flow to part of the brain. The scan shows no bleeding.
opts.mark: Explains the diagnosis in plain language

opts.t: There's a clot-dissolving drug. Given within 4½ hours, about 1 extra person in every 10 treated recovers with little or no disability. The main risk is bleeding in the brain — about 6 in 100 — which can be serious or fatal.
opts.mark: Explains benefits and risks with numbers

opts.t: It's a magic drug with no side effects.

turns.line: That's a big risk… can I think about it tomorrow?

opts.t: I understand. The benefit falls every minute, and after 4½ hours it isn't given. Overall, many more people are helped than harmed. What would you like to do?
opts.mark: Explains time dependence and supports her decision

qs.q: Time window for IV thrombolysis from onset?

wrong: 0.9 mg/kg over 1 hour, 10% as a bolus (max 90 mg)

qs.q: BP before thrombolysis must be below…

badge.name: Time Is Brain
badge.flavor: 4½ hours, BP under 185/110, CTA for the big clot.

cards.q: IV thrombolysis window for acute ischaemic stroke?
options: 24 hours from onset in all patients
1.5 mg/kg over 1 hour, 20% as a bolus
0.6 mg/kg, max 60 mg, 15% as a bolus

cards.why: Up to 24 h with imaging selection.

cards.q: Which is a contraindication to thrombolysis?
options: Age over 80 years with atrial fibrillation
cards.why: Age and diabetes are no longer absolute exclusions.
